description: An unofficial backport of Create Fly to Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric. No Fabric API required; Create's artwork is fetched from your own copy rather than bundled.

mods.name: Create: Godri
mods.description: Create for Fabric. This build is an unofficial backport to Minecraft 1.21.1 by Daniel Godri Neto; Create Fly itself is by ZurrTum, and Create by the Create Team. Create's artwork is All Rights Reserved and none of it is in this jar or this repository: on first launch the mod offers to fetch all 4,925 files from the Create Team's own release page. The only files under assets/create/ here are this port's own translations and item model definitions.

releases.notes:
First release of the 1.21.1 backport.

**Requires:** Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader 0.16.10+, Java 21+. Fabric API is **not** required.

---

## Before you install

Create's artwork belongs to the Create Team and is All Rights Reserved. **None of it is in this
jar.** On first launch the mod shows a setup screen and offers to fetch all 4,925 files from the
Create Team's own Modrinth release, about 20 MB. It verifies the download against the checksum
Modrinth published, copies the artwork out, and deletes the download.

Nothing is uploaded, no account is involved, and no server other than Modrinth is contacted. You can
instead point the setup screen at a Create jar you already have, or decline and leave Create switched
off. You only do this once.

The only files under `assets/create/` in this jar are 44 translations and 17 item model definitions,
both of which are this port's own work.

## What works

- Create's blocks, items, contraptions, recipes and ponder scenes
- With and without Fabric API. Both start with 2818 recipes, no tag or recipe errors
- Dedicated server
- Sodium and Iris (shaders disable Flywheel's optimisations, as upstream)
- Compiled-in compatibility for CC: Tweaked, Trinkets, Accessories and Cardinal Components

## Saving and loading

Backporting the storage layer was the largest single risk in this port, because a mistake there
loses your build silently rather than crashing. It is verified three ways:

- an automated round-trip of the storage layer itself, 46 checks
- an automated save, server restart and reload of 14 Create blocks, whose block-entity data comes
  back byte-identical
- a hand-played test: a deployer, depot, item vault and belt holding items, a schematicannon loaded
  with gunpowder and a schematic, and an assembled contraption — saved, the game fully closed and
  reopened, everything intact and the contraption still assembled

## Not in this build

- **Recipe viewer integration.** REI 16.x for 1.21.1 differs too much from the 20.x the upstream code
  targets, and EIV has no 1.21.1 build. Recipes work; you just cannot browse them in a viewer.
- **ModernFix** integration. No 1.21.1 Fabric build of `modernfix-mvus`.
- **Create's commands**, which upstream has not implemented either.
- **Slippery blocks affecting leashed entities.** 1.21.1's leash physics has no ground-friction term
  to hook into.
- The linked controller's redstone torch, whose model could not be established as fetchable.

## Known limitations

- **Do not open worlds made with other versions.** Data loading changed across these versions and
  data can be lost. This applies to worlds from other Minecraft versions or other Create builds, not
  to worlds made with this one.
- No full progression playthrough has been done, so later-game machinery is less exercised than the
  basics. Back up anything you would be sad to lose.

## Reporting problems

Report bugs on **this** repository's issue tracker, not to simibubi, the Create Team, NeoForge
Create, or ZurrTum. They did not write this port and cannot fix it. A useful report has your
`latest.log`, your Fabric Loader version, and your mod list.

## Credits

Create is by **simibubi and the Create Team**. Create Fly, which this backports, is by **ZurrTum**:
the architecture, the Yarn mappings work and the no-Fabric-API design are all theirs. Flywheel and
Vanillin are by **Engine-Room**, Ponder by **the Ponder project**.

This is an unofficial, community port. It is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any of them.
